fatal_errors: The proposed material is tempered martensitic steel rather than the target AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy.
It treats the conventional grain-boundary impurity-segregation mechanism as the answer, although that mechanism is the baseline contrast in the target study.
It omits the FCC+B2 initial microstructure, enhanced L12 ordering, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, and phase-boundary-driven plastic instability.
It does not identify the approximately 600°C embrittlement condition or the approximately 750°C ductility-recovery condition.
The experiment conflates thermal-aging temperature with mechanical-test temperature, so it would not cleanly test the aging-induced transition described by the target.
explanation: The hypothesis captures only the generic shape of a ductile–brittle–ductile response and offers a testable segregation correlation. It otherwise answers with the conventional-alloy phenomenon that the prompt uses as a contrast, rather than reconstructing the unexpected transition in as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1. The target transition arises after intermediate-temperature aging: maximum L12 ordering and jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary density near 600°C elevate slip resistance and concentrate stress, whereas reduced ordering and ductile transition zones near 750°C restore ductility. The proposed impurity-segregation account therefore disagrees on material, conditions, structural mediator, mechanism, and discriminating observations.
